1.title: Security Models and Microsoft Defender for Cloud
1.text: Welcome to Module ten: Security Models and Microsoft Defender for Cloud. It covers the exam area Describe Azure architecture and services. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Describe the concept of Zero Trust. Describe the purpose of the defense-in-depth model. Describe the purpose of Microsoft Defender for Cloud. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Describe Azure architecture and services (thirty-five to forty percent). Exam format: forty-five minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official A Z nine hundred study guide, current skills measured.

1.title: Zero Trust
1.text: Zero Trust. Zero Trust is a security model that does not trust anything by default, even inside the corporate network. Every request is treated as if it came from an open network. The three guiding principles. Verify explicitly. Always authenticate and authorize using all available data: identity, location, device health, service, data classification, anomalies. Use least-privilege access. Give only the access needed, limited in time and scope (just-in-time, just-enough access). Assume breach. Design as if an attacker is already inside: segment access, encrypt data, monitor and detect threats.

1.title: Zero Trust, continued
1.text: Zero Trust. The figure shows this: Zero Trust: verify explicitly, least privilege and assume breach.

1.title: Zero Trust, continued
1.text: Zero Trust. The old model was "trust everything inside the network perimeter". Zero Trust replaces it because users, devices and data are now everywhere (cloud, home, mobile). Exam tip: The slogan is "never trust, always verify." A question about M F A, device checks, least privilege and segmentation together describes Zero Trust.

1.title: Defense in depth
1.text: Defense in depth. Defense in depth uses multiple layers of protection, so if one layer fails the next still protects the data. It aims to slow an attacker and limit damage. Physical security. Protects: Datacenter buildings and hardware. Azure examples: Microsoft datacenter controls. Identity and access. Protects: Who can sign in and what they can do. Azure examples: Microsoft Entra I D, M F A, Conditional Access, R B A C. Perimeter. Protects: The edge of the network from large attacks. Azure examples: D dos (distributed denial of service) protection, Azure Firewall.

1.title: Defense in depth, continued
1.text: Defense in depth. Network. Protects: Traffic between resources. Azure examples: Network security groups, segmentation, private endpoints. Compute. Protects: Virtual machines and hosts. Azure examples: Patching, endpoint protection, restricted access to V Ms. Application. Protects: App code and A P Is. Azure examples: Secure development, secrets in a vault, app firewalls. Data. Protects: Stored information (the thing to protect). Azure examples: Encryption, access control, backup. The data is at the center and the layers wrap around it. Exam tip: The layers go physical to identity and access to perimeter to network to compute to application to data. The question may ask which layer a service belongs to: Entra I D equals identity and access, D dos protection and firewall equals perimeter, N S G equals network, encryption equals data.

1.title: Microsoft Defender for Cloud
1.text: Microsoft Defender for Cloud. Microsoft Defender for Cloud is a cloud-native application protection platform that does two jobs: it assesses your security posture and it protects workloads from threats. It works for Azure, on-premises (hybrid) and other clouds (multicloud).

1.title: Microsoft Defender for Cloud, continued
1.text: Microsoft Defender for Cloud. Cloud security posture management (C S P M). Continuously assesses your resources against security best practices, gives a Secure Score and recommendations to fix weaknesses. Cloud workload protection (C W P). Detects and responds to threats against your workloads with Defender plans for servers, storage, databases, containers and more. Regulatory compliance view. Shows how your resources measure against compliance standards. Multicloud and hybrid. The same view for Azure, on-premises machines (with Azure Arc) and other clouds. Secure Score: a percentage that shows how well your resources follow security recommendations; higher is better. Fixing recommendations raises it.

1.title: Microsoft Defender for Cloud, continued
1.text: Microsoft Defender for Cloud. Recommendations list what to fix and how, ranked by impact. The foundational posture features are free; advanced protection plans are paid. Exam tip: Posture and recommendations and score to Defender for Cloud. Threat protection for V Ms, storage, sequel to Defender for Cloud's Defender plans. Hybrid and multicloud protection to Defender for Cloud (with Azure Arc).

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors verifies every request using identity, device health and location, gives users only needed access and assumes attackers may already be inside. Which model is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Zero Trust. Verify explicitly, least privilege and assume breach are the Zero Trust principles.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which layer of defense in depth does Microsoft Entra I D with M F A protect? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Identity and access. Sign-in control and access are the identity and access layer.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. What is the main idea of defense in depth? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Multiple layers of protection so a failure in one does not expose everything. Layers slow attackers and limit damage when a layer fails.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which tool shows a Secure Score and recommendations for improving the security of Azure, on-premises and other cloud resources? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Microsoft Defender for Cloud. Defender for Cloud assesses posture, scores it and recommends fixes across hybrid and multicloud.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which Zero Trust principle says to limit users to the minimum access they need? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Use least-privilege access. Least privilege restricts access in scope and time.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which layer includes protecting the network edge from a distributed denial-of-service attack? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Perimeter. D dos protection and firewalls defend the perimeter.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the slogan of Zero Trust? Answer: Never trust, always verify. Question two. Name the three Zero Trust principles. Answer: Verify explicitly, use least-privilege access, assume breach. Question three. Name the seven layers of defense in depth in order. Answer: Physical, identity and access, perimeter, network, compute, application, data.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does Defender for Cloud's Secure Score show? Answer: How well your resources follow security recommendations; higher is better. Question five. Which two jobs does Defender for Cloud do? Answer: Posture management (assess and recommend) and workload protection (detect threats). Question six. Can Defender for Cloud cover non-Azure resources? Answer: Yes, on-premises (hybrid) and other clouds (multicloud).

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Zero Trust: never trust, always verify; verify explicitly, least privilege, assume breach. Defense in depth: layers: physical, identity and access, perimeter, network, compute, application, data. Layer examples: Entra I D or M F A equals identity; D dos and firewall equals perimeter; N S G equals network; encryption equals data. Defender for Cloud: posture (Secure Score, recommendations) plus threat protection; Azure, on-premises and other clouds. In the next module, we continue the course.
